en: The Hymn on the Method of the Twelve Causes. Homage to the Buddha Śākyamuni. (1) To the compassionate Śākya [Buddha], skilled in means...
I bow to this Lord of the Śākyas, who has destroyed the hostile Mārasena of his lineage, whose body is as beautiful as Mount Meru of gold.
He who, having first generated the mind of enlightenment and being endowed with both the accumulations of wisdom and merit,
manifests here today through sublime displays.
I praise the Lord of the World who has been born.
(2) Having led the gods [to liberation] and knowing that the time had come, he descended even from the world of the gods.
I bow to the family that beheld him entering the womb like an elephant, even as Māyādevī looked on;
I bow with certainty to that son of the Śākyas, who at the completion of ten months was honored by Brahmā and Indra, possessed of excellent marks, and destined for the lineage of awakening. 3.
Having subdued all those who were full of egoism, he seized the powerful youth who was displaying his artistic skill upon the body of Nṛsiṃha in Magadha.
I pay homage to the one who performs incomparable deeds, who,
for the sake of following the Dharma in the world, first established skillfulness in the means for abandoning faults and attaining long life. ||4|| (4)
I bow to him who dwells within the inner apartments and is intent upon the protection of the kingdom. ||5||
Having perceived the essencelessness of worldly existence,
he abandoned his home and departed by way of the sky; seeing him thus ordaining himself, [he followed].
I bow down facing the pure caitya.
(5) Having realized that the attainment of enlightenment comes through effort alone,
he practiced austerities for six years.
I bow to him who, at the edge of the Nairañjanā, reached the further shore of vigor and attained the supreme meditative absorption. ||7||
To make his beginningless efforts meaningful,
he sat beneath the Bodhi tree in Magadha,
bound in the cross-legged posture, having attained immovable awakening.
I bow to him who brings about the attainment of perfect enlightenment. (6) Having quickly beheld the world with compassion,
[he taught] in excellent places such as Vārāṇasī and others.
I bow to the one who turns the wheel of Dharma for those to be trained and leads them into the Threefold Discipline. ||9||
Then, in order to subdue the six non-Buddhist teachers and other evil-viewed ones such as Devadatta,
he indeed tamed Māra at Vārāṇasī.
I bow to the Sage Jayanta,
who, having displayed his matchless virtues throughout the three worlds,
performed the great miracle at Śrāvastī. ||10|| (7)
I bow to him who brings prosperity to the Teaching and is well-honored by the realms of gods and humans. ||11||
In order to swiftly urge on those who are indolent upon the pure ground of the city of Kauśī,
he abandoned his immortal body, which was as firm as a diamond.
I bow to him who has gone to final nirvāṇa;
for even though he is truly immortal,
future beings may thereby obtain merit.
I bow to him who, having at that time transformed many elements, bestows the eightfold elements. ||13||
By means of such merits arising from the praise of the summary of the playful activities of the Blessed One, the Teacher,
may even this conduct of all sentient beings [be purified]. (9)
May it be exactly like the conduct of the Sugata. ||14||
